quote: zeige, dass dieselbe [-einer Potenz-] im wesentlichen die Diskriminante der Diskriminante ist.
english: Show that the same [the functional determinant of the problem] is essentially the discriminant of the discriminant.
topic: Hilbert notes lecture plans (reading elliptic functions following Liouville, and a course on pure geometry with axioms, Euclidean geometry, analysis situs and projective geometry), a plan to study when two solutions of his discriminant problem coincide, and a remark that an irrational number contains nothing infinite.

triage.modern_statement: The note can't be pinned down to one precise statement, because 'the problem' and its 'functional determinant' (Jacobian) are not defined on the page. The likeliest reading: take a map built from a binary form, or a family of forms, whose discriminant locus is being studied. The claim would be that its Jacobian equals the discriminant of that discriminant (the discriminant of the discriminant polynomial, taken in one of its variables), raised to some power and up to unimportant factors. Put another way, the place where the map degenerates would coincide with the singular locus of the discriminant hypersurface (its cusp and double-point parts). This is a reconstruction, not something Hilbert wrote.
triage.answered_by: I found no source that addresses this exact claim. Two pieces of related work exist: (a) Hilbert's own paper 'Über die Singularitäten der Diskriminantenfläche' (Math. Ann. 30, 1887, pp. 437–441), which studies the singular locus of the discriminant surface of binary forms; (b) modern work on 'iterated discriminants', i.e. discriminants of discriminants and how they factor: Lazard & McCallum (MEGA 2007; J. Symb. Comput. 44, 2009), Busé & Mourrain ('Explicit factors of some iterated resultants and discriminants', Math. Comp. 78, 2009), and later papers on iterated and mixed discriminants (arXiv 2101.11571).

evidence.claim: Hilbert published 'Über die Singularitäten der Diskriminantenfläche' in Math. Ann. 30, 437–441 (1887). It is the published paper closest to this diary topic and is still cited, for example in a 1919 Math. Ann. paper on a new property of discriminants and resultants of binary forms.
A 1919 Math. Ann. article on discriminants and resultants of binary forms (vol. 79) cites Hilbert's 1887 paper on the discriminant surface.
Lazard and McCallum published 'Iterated discriminants' (J. Symb. Comput. 44(9), 1176–1193, 2009), which studies discriminants of discriminants.
A 2009 Math. Comp. paper analyses iterated univariate resultant and discriminant constructions applied to multivariate polynomials and identifies explicit factors.
Recent work defines a multivariate iterated discriminant, described as computing the discriminant of a discriminant, and proves it is always divisible by the mixed discriminant.

triage.why: The page doesn't say which 'discriminant problem' is meant or what its 'functional determinant' is, so the conjecture can't be stated precisely or matched to a specific later result. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems or the 24th problem. The general theme, how the discriminant of a discriminant factors and how it relates to the singularities of the discriminant locus, was taken up by Hilbert himself in 1887. Computer algebra researchers have also studied it since about 2007 under the name 'iterated discriminants', and work continued at least into 2021–2023. None of the sources I found says it proves or refutes this particular diary claim. So I can only call the topic related, not say the question was answered, and whether this exact question is active today is unclear.
